questions.q: What are the standard parts of a properly formatted journal entry?
options: Only a dollar amount, nothing else
A supplier name and a tax ID number
A date, one or more debit lines, one or more credit lines, and a memo
A list of all accounts in the chart of accounts
questions.explain: A journal entry includes a date, debit lines (first), credit lines (indented beneath), and a memo describing the transaction.

questions.q: What distinguishes a compound journal entry from a simple one?
options: A compound entry has more than two lines total, while a simple entry has exactly one debit and one credit
A compound entry never has to balance
A simple entry can have unlimited debit lines
Compound entries are only used for cash transactions
questions.explain: Simple entries have exactly one debit and one credit line; compound entries have more lines but must still balance in total.

questions.q: Millbrook Bread Co. buys an $8,000 oven using $2,000 cash and a $6,000 loan. What is the correct compound entry?
options: Debit Equipment $8,000; Credit Cash $8,000
Debit Equipment $8,000; Credit Cash $2,000; Credit Notes Payable $6,000
Debit Cash $2,000; Debit Notes Payable $6,000; Credit Equipment $8,000
Debit Equipment $2,000; Debit Notes Payable $6,000; Credit Cash $8,000
questions.explain: Equipment (an asset) increases by the full $8,000; Cash decreases by $2,000 and Notes Payable (liability) increases by $6,000 — totals balance at $8,000 on each side.

questions.q: Why does a journal entry's memo matter?
options: It is purely decorative and has no practical use
It determines whether the entry is a debit or a credit
It replaces the need for a date on the entry
It explains why the entry was recorded, which is crucial for anyone reviewing it later
questions.explain: A clear memo helps anyone reviewing the entry later understand what it represents and why it was recorded.

questions.q: What does the Oracle Fusion Subledger Accounting engine fundamentally do, in terms of this lesson's concepts?
options: It eliminates the need for journal entries entirely
It only handles compound entries, never simple ones
It is a rules engine that turns subledger transactions into correctly formed journal entries with this same date/debit/credit/memo anatomy
It has no relationship to journal entries at all
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting takes transactions from subledgers like Payables and Receivables and turns them into properly structured journal entries behind the scenes.
